the differential cross sections for the He–C2 H2 system were computed using a new ab initio potential energy surface, and the resulting data are in excellent agreement to experiment, which proves that the potential is indeed very good.
the SAPT He–C2 H2 potential is very accurate, and that the state-resolved close-coupling results for this potential agree very well with experiment.
the SAPT He–C2D potential is very accurate and that the close-coupling approach is a reliable and efficient tool for computing state-to-state cross sections for He–CnH2n+2 scattering.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a comprehensive study of the interaction potential of He and C2H2, and its application to state-to-state cross sections, total differential cross sections, and energy loss spectra.
the development of an ab initio interaction potential for the scattering system He-C2H2 and its application to state-to-state differential and total cross sections.
the development and application of ab initio methods for the computation of potential energy surfaces (PESs) of van der Waals complexes.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the present results are the most accurate theoretical data for He +C 2H2 scattering so far.
the SAPT interaction potential is the best ab initio potential for He–CnH2n+2 (n=2,3,4) systems available today.
the SAPT approach is a reliable method to obtain ab initio potentials for He–CnHn systems.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the SAPT method is able to provide accurate intermolecular potentials for light–light systems, and that these can be used to calculate scattering data of the same quality as experiment.
the SAPT method is able to provide reliable intermolecular potentials for the calculation of scattering cross sections for light–polyatomic systems.

a potential energy surface computed by SAPT is capable to reproduce state-to-state cross sections for the scattering of a small molecule with a rare gas atom, and that the agreement with experiment is excellent.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the close-coupling method is a very powerful and accurate tool to compute cross sections for polyatomic molecules, which are notoriously difficult to treat by conventional methods such as the classical-trajectory or quasi-classical trajectory methods.
the SAPT method is a viable alternative to the widely used dispersion-corrected density-functional theory approach, as it yields accurate results without any empirical parameters.
the close-coupling method can be used to predict accurate cross sections for complex molecules.
